provenance.l: ispace, results of the HAKUTO-R Mission 1 landing (26 May 2023): descent began from about 100 km at 00:40 JST 26 Apr (15:40 UTC 25 Apr); deceleration was completed as planned and the lander was below 1 m/s vertically at about 5 km. Passing a crater rim about 3 km high, the measured altitude jumped; the software judged the altimeter abnormal and discarded it, so the lander believed it was at 0 m while about 5 km up. After the scheduled landing time (16:43 UTC) it kept descending slowly until its propellant ran out, then fell freely. The model starts there: the braking from orbit is not drawn
NASA LRO: the impact site at 47.581 N, 44.094 E, at least four large pieces of debris (LROC, 23 May 2023)

HAKUTO-R Series 1 lander: dry mass about 340 kg (ispace design release); about 1,000 kg fuelled at launch (Spaceflight Now). The mass left at 5 km, the propellant left for the slow descent and the engine's specific impulse are not published: estimates. No impact time or speed is published; the speed shown (about 126 m/s) is a free fall from about 4.9 km
